diagonal_weighted_reflection_thue_audit.summary: TICKET-254 proves two exact route no-go theorems and two partial theorems while leaving all four parent conjectures open.

riemann.declared_proposition: For every N>=1 there is a bounded positive self-adjoint operator A_N on l2(Z), with <A_N e_n,e_n>=1 for every Fourier basis vector, but <A_N d_N,d_N>=0 for d_N=(2N+1)^(-1/2)sum_(|n|<=N)e_n. On the L=2N+1 packet block take A_N=L/(L-1)I-J/(L-1), and take the identity off that block. Its packet-block spectrum is {0,L/(L-1)}. Thus even a uniform strictly positive Fourier diagonal does not imply Dirichlet-packet domination without off-diagonal information.
riemann.mathematical_argument: Every diagonal entry of L/(L-1)I-J/(L-1) is one. The all-ones vector is killed because J has eigenvalue L there; on its orthogonal complement J is zero and the eigenvalue is L/(L-1)>0. Direct sum with the identity gives a bounded positive self-adjoint operator on l2(Z). The normalized all-ones block vector is d_N, so its energy is zero. This counterexample addresses diagonal-only inference, not the actual Guinand-Weil form.

reproducible_computation.algorithm: exact Fraction evaluation of the two eigenspaces of an equicorrelated finite block embedded in l2(Z)
reproducible_computation.complexity: O(number of replay blocks); the all-N construction is algebraic

riemann.finite_computation_boundary: 8 exact rational blocks replay the all-N algebraic construction.

route_decision.discard: inferring a positive Dirichlet-packet lower bound from uniform positivity of Fourier diagonal entries alone
parked: actual Weil-form block matrices and their off-diagonal row sums
route_decision.retain: the need for quantitative off-diagonal control on actual Weil blocks

riemann.claim_boundary: No RH proof or disproof; one exact no-go for diagonal-only packet domination.

collatz.declared_proposition: For every finite set Q of primes q>5, every nonnegative weights w_q, and arbitrary pairs (U_q,V_q) in F_q^2, let D_q=5U_q-3V_q and C_q(D)=sum_(h=1)^(q-1)exp(2pi ihD/q). Then sum_q w_q[(1+C_q(D_q))/q-1_(U_q=V_q=0)] equals exactly sum_q w_q 1_(D_q=0,(U_q,V_q)!=(0,0)). Every summand is nonnegative. Hence nonnegative cross-prime averaging of the complete detector creates no cancellation or smoothing; bounding it is exactly the original weighted incidence problem.
collatz.mathematical_argument: Additive-character orthogonality gives (1+C_q(D))/q=1_(D=0) pointwise. Subtract the origin indicator and multiply by w_q>=0. Summing preserves equality and nonnegativity. Therefore a claimed cancellation estimate for this normalized complete detector cannot be an independent route to canonical slope avoidance. Signed incomplete kernels may still contain information and are not ruled out.

reproducible_computation.algorithm: exact q^2 Fermat quotients, integer character dichotomy, and Fraction-weighted identities
reproducible_computation.complexity: O(sum log q) modular multiplications for canonical rows; the weighted identity is algebraic for arbitrary finite Q

collatz.finite_computation_boundary: 48 detector rows and 12 exact weighted rows replay the universal identity.
collatz.logical_limit: The theorem blocks only normalized complete detectors with nonnegative weights; it says nothing about a genuinely signed incomplete transform or canonical occurrence.

route_decision.discard: using any nonnegative weighted cross-prime average of the normalized complete slope detector as an independent cancellation statistic
parked: signed incomplete character kernels with a proved recovery inequality
route_decision.retain: character truncation or another signed transform not identical to incidence

collatz.claim_boundary: No Collatz proof or counterexample; one exact no-go for the proposed cross-prime complete-average implementation.

goldbach.declared_proposition: Let q>=5 be prime, m be even with q not dividing m, and c_r be the cyclic coefficients of (1-X)^m modulo X^q-1. Suppose the tail is zero-residue compatible, set t=1-c_0 and T=qt, and put r=m mod q. Let kappa_q(r) be the global prime index of the second prime congruent to r modulo q. If T>=kappa_q(r), then the tail cannot be realized by the actual prime prefix. Indeed c_r=c_0 by even reflection, so the forced count N*_r=c_r+t is one, whereas the first T primes contain at least two primes in residue r.
goldbach.mathematical_argument: Writing a_j=(-1)^j binom(m,j), the involution j->m-j gives a_(m-j)=(-1)^m a_j. Folding modulo q therefore yields c_(m-r)=(-1)^m c_r. For even m and r=0 this says c_(m mod q)=c_0. Since q does not divide m, that residue is nonzero, and compatibility fixes its target count at c_0+(1-c_0)=1. If T reaches the second prime in that class, its actual prefix count is at least two, contradicting the TICKET-253 unique-prefix criterion. Odd m, q-divisible m, and T below the explicit threshold are not excluded by this argument.

reproducible_computation.algorithm: exact cyclic binomial folding plus deterministic enumeration of the first two primes in one nonzero residue class
reproducible_computation.complexity: O(sum m + sum kappa log kappa) integer operations for the finite replay; the reflection-threshold theorem is algebraic

goldbach.finite_computation_boundary: 480 even pairs scanned; 50 compatible non-q-divisible rows have exact two-prime certificates.
goldbach.logical_limit: The reflection theorem excludes only even m with q not dividing m and a verified prefix threshold. It is not a uniform theorem for every compatible tail and does not prove strong Goldbach.

route_decision.discard: treating compatible even cyclotomic tails with q not dividing m as unconstrained after the unique-prefix reduction
parked: reflection rows below the second-residue-prime threshold
route_decision.retain: the exact reflection identity and second-residue-prime prefix obstruction

goldbach.claim_boundary: No strong Goldbach proof or counterexample; one infinite conditional exclusion theorem and finite certificates for selected compatible tails.

twin_prime.declared_proposition: Positive integer solutions of x^2-2=y^17 are equivalent to admissible integer points on seventeen explicit homogeneous degree-17 equations. For 0<=j<17 write (1+sqrt(2))^j=a_j+b_j sqrt(2) and define A_j(u,v)+B_j(u,v)sqrt(2)=(a_j+b_j sqrt(2))(u+v sqrt(2))^17. A solution exists iff for some j,u,v, B_j(u,v)=1, A_j(u,v)>0, and y=(-1)^j(u^2-2v^2)>0; then x=A_j(u,v).
twin_prime.mathematical_argument: First y is odd: if y and x were even then v_2(x^2-2)=1, not a multiple of 17. Thus the conjugate factors x+sqrt(2) and x-sqrt(2) are coprime in Z[sqrt(2)]. This ring is norm-Euclidean, hence a UFD, so x+sqrt(2)=epsilon alpha^17. Its units are +/- (1+sqrt(2))^n; absorb a 17th unit power and the sign into alpha to leave the unique twist j modulo 17. Comparing sqrt(2) coefficients gives B_j=1, and norms give y=(-1)^j(u^2-2v^2). The converse follows by multiplying out and taking norms. The reduction is exact, but no global integral-point exclusion for the seventeen equations is proved.

reproducible_computation.algorithm: exact quadratic-ring binary exponentiation, explicit homogeneous coefficient evaluation, and integer norm identities
reproducible_computation.complexity: O(17 R^2 log 17) quadratic-ring multiplications for box radius R=12; the equivalence is algebraic for all integers

twin_prime.finite_computation_boundary: 17 exact polynomials and 10608 integer grid cases verify coefficient and norm identities; global integral points remain open.
twin_prime.logical_limit: The reduction has seventeen equations but solves none globally. The finite box is only an implementation audit and cannot use the prior y>10^1000 bound as a proof.

route_decision.discard: treating x^2-2=y^17 as one opaque two-variable exponential equation without exposing its finite unit-twist classes
parked: global integral-point exclusion on the seventeen coefficient-one Thue equations
route_decision.retain: the exact Z[sqrt(2)] factorization and seventeen explicit homogeneous equations

twin_prime.claim_boundary: No twin-prime proof or counterexample; one exact exponent-17 Thue reduction with no admissible point found in a finite box.
